images.creator: staticd
images.title: Onion root mitosis
images.sourceDescription: Author identifies stained onion-root-tip squash microscopy and claims the photographed material as own work.
images.changes: None. Original JPEG bytes retained; no AI reconstruction, recolouring, sharpening or pixel removal.
images.attribution: Onion root mitosis — staticd, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0. Original image, unchanged.
images.requiredAttributionPlacement: Visible adjacent creator, linked source and linked license, with unchanged-image statement; keep these notices in every later authorized derivative.
images.scienceReview: Full original-resolution file inspected. Actual stained cells show variable chromosome condensation, separate chromosome groups and ambiguous boundaries/planes. Use evidence descriptions and uncertainty rather than asserting that every cell has an unambiguous phase label.
limitations: This selected field is not a representative random sample for estimating time in each phase.
No reliable calibrated scale is supplied; do not add an invented magnification or scale bar.
Projection, staining and cell overlap limit chromosome counting and fine stage distinctions.
The synthetic 72/12/6/4/6 counts are a separate teaching dataset and were not counted from this image.
A digital image task demonstrates observation/reasoning, not handling a microscope or preparing a biological specimen.
images.learnerPrompt: Inspect the original field, then describe the indicated region before proposing a stage. Identify the chromosome arrangement you can actually see. State one uncertainty and compare with the taught phase model. Do not force a label when the features are insufficient.

regions.observable: Two compact stained groups are separated within the outlined cell region.
regions.provisionalInterpretation: Consistent with a later mitotic separation stage. Condensed separated groups support anaphase; without clear daughter-nucleus or cell-plate evidence, distinguish that from a confident telophase identification.
regions.acceptReasoning: Describe two separated chromosome groups and connect separation to the model. Accept a qualified late-mitotic interpretation with evidence and a stated missing feature.

regions.observable: Prominent condensed, thread-like chromosomes occupy the central cell region; one clear equatorial plate is not established by this view.
regions.provisionalInterpretation: Condensation is consistent with a mitotic cell. The exact prophase/prometaphase/metaphase boundary is uncertain in this view.
regions.acceptReasoning: Use visible condensation, avoid calling two daughter groups where none is clear, and explain what alignment or separation evidence would distinguish the stages.

images.pixelPolicy: Render the original intact. Region indicators may be separate HTML/SVG overlays and must be identified as course annotations; enlargement must retain access to the whole original field.

sourceComparison.suppliedTextbook: Chapter 16 physical page 14, printed 557, Figure 16.8 remains the historical five-phase source reference.
sourceComparison.decision: Use the openly licensed original as an additional learner observation field with explicit uncertainty. Keep textbook reference and phase teaching; do not re-label the synthetic count table as observed from either image.
